reuse.why: All link handlers share one new guard helper and Fintegra reuses findOrCreateBank/syncAccount/handleSyncResponse, but the local-unlink update is re-written instead of reusing unlinkAccount's logic and the Fintegra link/download functions are copies of the Akahu ones.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a near line-for-line copy of linkAkahuAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions, and the replace branch repeats unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount field list.

placement.why: The guard sits in accounts/app.ts next to the link handlers and the download in sync.ts beside the other providers, matching the tree's layering, though the guard mixes validation with a mutating unlink.

scope.why: Changes stay on the requested link/sync paths; the two client edits are type-forced registry entries, plus release notes.

maintainability.why: A single guard for every provider is good, but its name (assertBankAccountNotLinked) hides a closed-account check and a side-effecting unlink, and the per-provider copy pattern grows by another full copy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked replace branch writes the unlink fields with db.updateAccount instead of going through (a local part of) unlinkAccount in accounts/app.ts

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (Fintegra link vs Akahu link, Fintegra download vs Akahu download, unlink field update) are verbatim, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked in accounts/app.ts: step 3 adds a closed-target branch, step 4 adds the replaceExistingLink parameter and a branch that unlinks other accounts; all six link handlers call it.
